name: Fatigue
def: How tired the fighter is by night, 0 to 100.
why: From 80 the next morning trains at 60%, and a camp that peaks at 80 or more fails its fatigue line.

name: Condition
def: The fighter card's freshness: 100 minus her fatigue.
why: It is fatigue turned round, so fatigue 20 shows as condition 80.

name: Training load
def: This week's training hours against a usual week.
why: Over 1.3 the injury risk climbs, and from 1.5 it is 3 times the usual.

name: Camp phase
def: BASE, BUILD, PEAK or TAPER, counted back from fight night.
why: The phase writes the coach's week: volume in BUILD, the hardest week at PEAK, light in TAPER.

name: Twist card
def: The week's surprise, dealt on Monday.
why: About 1 week in 4 it has no choice; otherwise answer it by Monday or the coach's pick stands.

name: Morning session
def: The day's training card, run Light, Normal or Hard.
why: A morning is a fifth of a focused week's gain, times 0.6 Light, 1.0 Normal or 1.3 Hard.

name: Pad night
def: An evening drilling moves and combinations on the pads with the coach.
why: Each pad night gives 240 drill minutes, split over the cards on it.

name: Weight cut
def: Eating 500 kcal a day under her need to reach the class limit.
why: About 0.45 kg comes off a week (7,700 kcal a kg), plus 0.05 kg a day in fight week.

name: Injury
def: Time out hurt, from a bout or a training week.
why: While out she gets a quarter of the training gains; up to 2 weeks is minor, up to 4 moderate.

name: Weapon
def: A move at mastery 30 or more.
why: Past the first 4 weapons, each one adds 0.3 power on the night, up to 0.9.

name: Mastery
def: How well a move is drilled, 0 to 100: Raw, Usable, Sharp, Signature.
why: Technique and Ring IQ cap it; a week without drilling costs 0.75, never below 30 once reached.

name: Morale
def: The fighter's mood, 0 to 100: Fired up, Steady, Flat or Low.
why: It starts at 60; a win adds 8 and a loss costs 12.

name: Trust
def: The fighter's mood, read as trust in the corner.
why: Fired up takes in 105% of the corner's calls, Steady 100%, Flat 85% and Low 70%.

name: Fighter goal
def: What the fighter wants done by a deadline, first set when she signs.
why: A new signing wants a bout booked and conditioning up 3.5 in 28 days; met is +10 morale, missed -20.

name: Potential
def: How good a fighter could become: stars before her trial, a number after.
why: Before her free Monday trial the stars are a range; a trial reads good at potential 80 or more.

name: Reputation
def: What the town thinks of the gym.
why: It sets how many members the gym can carry (48 plus 0.6 a point); a win adds 5, a loss costs 2.

name: Rankings
def: The region's amateurs in her division, best first.
why: She enters the table at 4 wins, and it sorts by wins minus losses.

name: National championships
def: A regional draw, then a national draw, for the amateur title.
why: She can enter with 5 bouts and 91 days registered, aged 19 to 40.

name: Belt
def: A grappler's rank: white, blue, purple, brown, black.
why: White to blue takes 200 classes and every syllabus move owned at mastery 30; each quarter earns a stripe.

name: Fight camp
def: The weeks of training set for a booked bout.
why: No camp costs 1.5 power on the night, and a camp needs at least 7 days to go.

name: Camp focus
def: The one stat a camp builds hardest.
why: It becomes the week's main morning session, and the camp's goal is that stat up 2.

name: Camp protocol
def: How hard the camp runs: Light, Standard or Hard.
why: Light, Standard and Hard run 3, 4 and 5 nights and multiply the focus stat's gain by 1.1, 1.2 and 1.35.

name: Peak camp
def: A camp that meets all three goal lines on fight night.
why: Weight made, the focus stat on target and fatigue kept under 80 give +1 to every stat that night.

name: Combination
def: A run of punches from the book or built in the Playbook.
why: It opens once every punch in it is at mastery 30; longer ones cost more energy a throw.

name: Plan line
def: A place in the ring, maybe a situation, and her answer there.
why: An answer that beats the opponent's game is worth up to 9 power an exchange, one that works 3; a wrong one costs 7.

name: Plan grade
def: The fight's verdict on your plan: good, mixed, wrong or no plan.
why: Good needs a mean edge of 1.5 an exchange; each point of edge is worth about 4.7% win chance.

name: Tape study
def: Watching the opponent's film in camp to open her hidden tells.
why: One tell opens on the camp's first day, then one every 2 days; each your plan answers adds 0.4 power, up to 1.2.

name: Weigh-in
def: The scale before the bout: the class limit plus 0.05 kg.
why: Miss it and the bout is off and the club pays $300 for the empty slot.

name: Heavy legs
def: Camp fatigue still in her legs on fight night.
why: Each fatigue point over 50 costs 2 energy at the first bell, up to 20.

name: Energy
def: The fighter's tank in the bout, 0 to 100.
why: Moving costs 18 a round; under 40 she tires and under 20 her punches lose force.

name: Exchange
def: A 30-second part of a round; a round has six.
why: Each is settled on its own, and corner shouts after the second in a round land at half.

name: Corner call
def: The instruction you shout from the corner.
why: A call that fits best is worth up to 15 power an exchange, an ok one 5; a wrong one costs 7 or more.

name: Habit
def: A fight habit the opponent can punish, like dropping the right after the jab.
why: A punished habit costs 6 power that exchange; the corner can fix one each minute.

name: Cutman
def: The corner man who closes cuts and brings down swollen eyes.
why: An open cut takes 1.5 times the damage; his work holds for the next round only.

name: Scorecards
def: Three judges score each round 10-9 to its winner.
why: An amateur bout is 3 rounds; a majority of the judges decides, and no majority is a draw.

name: Runway
def: Weeks the cash lasts at this week's net.
why: Under 8 weeks the cash turns amber; 8 weeks below $0 in a row close the gym.

name: Dues
def: Each member pays $35 a month; the gym keeps it by the week.
why: Members are the gym's steady income: about $8 a member a week.

name: Members
def: People who pay dues to train at the club.
why: Each week the count walks a quarter of the way to its target, at most 6; a win brings 8.

name: Month-end bill
def: Wages and upkeep, paid every four weeks.
why: It falls every 28 days, and time stops on the bill day so you see it land.

name: Coach
def: The staff member who runs the sessions and works the corner.
why: The sessional coach costs $450 a week and $1,000 to sign; with a coach, evening classes add $350 a week.

name: Stipend
def: The club's weekly pay to an amateur fighter.
why: Each amateur costs $250 a week; it stops when she turns pro.

name: Sponsor
def: A company that pays the club each week for its name on show.
why: Ironclad pays $250 a week from the start; Bow Road pays $150 after her first win.

name: Ticket cut
def: The club's share of the door at an amateur bout.
why: Each amateur bout pays the club $450; championship bouts pay none.

name: Pro debut
def: Her first pro bout, a small-hall show 4 weeks after she signs.
why: The offer comes at 7 wins and a top-3 ranking, or 9 wins; the club pays $230 licence plus $875 medicals.

name: Purse
def: What a pro is paid for a bout.
why: From her second pro bout it is $1,500, +$500 a pro win up to $3,000; the club keeps 25%.
